reports.label: Gallatin
reports.excerpt: The Gallatin has been fishing awfully well these past few days. Flows have been very steady and the water clarity has been great. Fishing deeper buckets right now has been a safe bet for finding a couple fish over there.

reports.label: Upper Madison
reports.excerpt: The Upper Madison has been fishing pretty well as of late. Streamer fishing has been pretty good on the right days, and midges are around in very good numbers on the surface. Dry fly fishing by Raynold's pass is always a good option if you are wade fishing over there.

reports.label: Lower Madison
reports.excerpt: The Lower Madison has been a good option recently. Fishing has been good throughout the day, and dry fly fishing has been great on the right days. Midges have been the most abundant food source up top, but BWOs are around as well.

reports.label: Missouri
reports.excerpt: The fishing on the Missouri has been fishing well lately. Fish have been eager to eat something moving, so stripping or dragging a streamer might produce a fish or two. If they're being a little more tight lipped try nymphing with a larger attractor and sow bug underneath.

reports.label: Yellowstone
reports.excerpt: The Yellowstone has been pretty darn good lately. Fish are holding in pretty deep water right now, so try changing depth before changing flies. Streamer fishing has been pretty decent on the warmer parts of the day, and nymphing is always good.

reports.label: Gallatin
reports.excerpt: We love the months of October and November on the Gallatin River near Big Sky and Bozeman. Flows are at base level in the canyon. Fishing is not just a morning game, and as temperatures drop, the afternoons can still be productive.

reports.label: Upper Madison
reports.excerpt: Hard to believe November is coming this weekend! Things are still fishing quite well so it is worth getting out there! The Upper Madison River near Ennis and towards West Yellowstone has been a consistent producer for us lately and is one of the best games around at the moment.

reports.label: Lower Madison
reports.excerpt: The fishing on the Lower Madison has been very good and should remain so as we get into November this weekend. The fish are definitely looking for big pieces of meat, including crayfish and baitfish.

reports.label: Missouri
reports.excerpt: November on the Missouri River means consistent dry fly fishing for head-hunting rising trout can be very good. But pick your moments and your sections wisely. Most of the Blue-Winged Olives right now are being spotted more in the canyon sections that are above Craig or below Cascade.

reports.label: Jefferson
reports.excerpt: Even though the Jefferson is very low, this is a good time to fish this river...but there are definitely options that have more fish. This is a low fish count river, so don’t expect a lot of numbers, and you really need to know exactly where these trout are holding, or it can be a long and slow day.

reports.label: Gallatin
reports.excerpt: Late October fishing is here, and the Gallatin is still a great option for getting out on the water. Cooler mornings and shorter days mean trout are starting to settle into slower, deeper water.

reports.label: Upper Madison
reports.excerpt: Walk Wade Stretch (Between the Lakes, Upriver of Lyon's Bridge, Downriver of Ennis): The Upper Madison is settling into its fall rhythm. Cooler nights and clear water have fish transitioning toward smaller fall food sources, with baetis becoming increasingly important.

reports.label: Lower Madison
reports.excerpt: The Lower Madison is fishing alright right now, but with the warmer temperatures, getting out early is definitely going to be your best bet. We’re expecting some cooler weather and possibly some precipitation this weekend, which could help bring water temperatures down a bit and make the canyon section worth a look.

reports.label: Yellowstone
reports.excerpt: The Yellowstone is settling into fall conditions. Recent rain has added some color, but the river is clearing quickly and looking good. Cooler mornings mean there’s no need to rush out at first light right now.

reports.label: Yellowstone
reports.excerpt: The Yellowstone has been fishing well, and the smaller rubberlegs have been producing consistently over the past couple of weeks. They show no signs of slowing down, and pretty much any color in a size 10–14 has been a great option.

reports.label: Yellowstone
reports.excerpt: Over the course of the last week, a series of rain events has pumped more mud into the Yellowstone River. As the week progresses, we should expect to see clearing and a return to some great fishing.

reports.label: Madison
reports.excerpt: Early Fall flows. She's a little skinny. This will change if/when the storm rolls in. Dropped back to prep for Fall brown trout flows, should stay here for the winter.

reports.label: Upper Madison
reports.excerpt: Well, the rain (and snow) had a good few days, but seems to be on its way out again. That fall chill is in the air, however, and seems to be here to stay, just like the hungry attitude of the fish!

reports.label: Missouri
reports.excerpt: We are looking forward to the month ahead. November is great fishing. One of the best parts of the month include the lack of anglers around. Another highlight is the fish that like to rise.
